components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Used for main calls to action like 'Resume' or 'Contact'.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #5E6470; color: #ffffff; padding: 16px 32px; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 16px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.3s ease; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.05); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #000000; box-shadow: 0 4px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); transform: translateY(-2px); }

narrative.overview: This system embraces a technical, analytical, and data-driven aesthetic. It prioritizes structure and clarity, utilizing a monotonous, restrained color palette to keep the focus on content and achievements. The design is layered and tactile, employing subtle glassmorphic surfaces, soft shadows, and gentle hover movements to create an interactive experience that feels responsive and polished.
keyCharacteristics: Large, friendly border radii contrasting with technical typography.

rules.name: The Monotonous Rule
rules.body: Stick to the grayscale and slate spectrum. Avoid introducing new vibrant accent colors; use opacity and contrast to create visual hierarchy.

rules.name: The Tactile Lift Rule
rules.body: Elements that can be interacted with should respond physically. When hovered, cards and buttons should lift slightly (-translate-y-1) and increase their shadow spread.

dos: Do use large border radii (24px - 32px) for structural containers to maintain the approachable feel.
Do apply backdrop-blur-md and semi-transparent backgrounds to cards to create depth against the solid background.
Do ensure physical, tactile transitions on interactive elements (e.g., -translate-y-1 on hover).
donts: Don't introduce vibrant or saturated colors outside of the monochrome/slate spectrum.
Don't use sharp, 0px border radii on structural elements.
Don't use solid, opaque backgrounds for cards; always retain a degree of glassmorphism.
